html:
SMTO-EXE-0058 — SMTO won't close that program because it's protected

GUID: 318574c0-cc2b-5ab8-b501-22901d2f1b85
Slug: desktop-protected-process
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • The program you asked SMTO to close or stop belongs to the system, to SMTO or its Gateway, or to another user, so SMTO refused. Nothing was closed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the running apps and make sure you chose an ordinary app that you opened yourself on that computer. SMTO only closes everyday apps owned by the signed-in user.
  2. If you really need to stop a system program, another user's program, SMTO itself or a program run with Python, ask the person who manages that computer to do it there directly. These programs are protected so SMTO can't break the computer or shut itself down.

What success looks like

  • SMTO closes the ordinary app you chose, or the computer's manager stops the protected program themselves.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO refuses an ordinary app you started yourself, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't run the Gateway as an administrator to get around this protection.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Process termination safeguards refused the target because it is critical, privileged, owned by another user, part of the Gateway/Server runtime or its parent processes, a Python/SMTO runtime executable, or could not be safely inspected.

What this means

  • Process termination safeguards classified the target as critical, privileged, foreign-owned, part of protected runtime ancestry, or could not safely inspect it. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Process termination safeguards classified the target as critical, privileged, foreign-owned, part of protected runtime ancestry, or could not safely inspect it.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the protected-target reason and workload ownership without weakening the guard or substituting a raw PID.

How to fix it

  • Choose a noncritical application owned by the Gateway's user. Processes.guard always refuses PIDs 0/1, the Gateway process and its parents, python/pypy/smto/gateway-agent executables, root/SYSTEM or other-user processes, well-known system services, Windows critical processes and targets it cannot inspect; handle those outside the Desktop capability.
  • Choose a noncritical user application. Gateway, controller, system and unclassifiable processes cannot be terminated by Desktop.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose a noncritical user application. Gateway, controller, system and unclassifiable processes cannot be terminated by Desktop.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported noncritical user application is selected, or its owner handles the protected process outside this capability.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
